prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which opened the field of moire quantum materials.

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the one candidate on the shortlist where a sharp theoretical prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, flat bands at a magic angle) was followed within seven years by an experimental discovery (correlated insulators and superconductivity, Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators) that nature did not have to give. A single tunable parameter, the twist angle, controls bandwidth and interaction strength, which is conceptually close to how a statistical physicist wants to explore a phase diagram. The phenomenology has been reproduced by many independent laboratories and carried over to other moire systems, so the discovery itself is firm even though the pairing mechanism is not. It gathered the broadest opening support (seven of eight members ranked it, three first places, six top-three), and the theory-plus-experiment trio is a natural three-person allocation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing and maturity: the field is under eight years old, the microscopic origin of superconductivity is unresolved, and device-to-device variability (twist-angle disorder) complicates comparison. A citation must therefore rest on the platform and the correlated states rather than on a settled mechanism. A second reservation is credit: the first author of the 2018 experiments, earlier twisted-bilayer theory, and other moire groups fall outside a three-name limit, so any allocation will be contested.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked B038 second but wonders whether the field has produced a stable enough body of results for a prize or whether a few more years of waiting are warranted, and he ranked dynamical mean-field theory (B037) first.
responses.response: I take the maturity worry seriously, but I would separate the mechanism from the discovery. The existence of flat-band-driven correlated insulators and superconductivity has been confirmed across many groups and platforms, and that is what a citation would rest on. Waiting for the pairing mechanism would tie recognition to a question that may stay open for decades. On B037 I disagree with ranking it first: I placed it last of my eight because DMFT is a method rather than a single discovery, I am uneasy about Metzner being outside the credited names, and the prize tradition for computational methods is thin. I accept its importance for correlated materials, but it does not displace B038.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked B038 first as a clear case of a prediction matched by nature, but flags that Yuan Cao as first author of the experiments and earlier twisted-graphene theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) raise allocation questions.
responses.response: I agree on the strength of the prediction-meets-experiment pattern and share the attribution concern. I would not remedy it by enlarging the credit, which the three-person limit forbids; the question is whether the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper is the decisive prediction, and I think it is, because it identified the magic angle and the quantitative flat-band condition rather than only the band-narrowing trend. Cao's role can be acknowledged in the citation text through the experimental discovery by Jarillo-Herrero's group, but I would hold the laureate set at the three names rather than reopen it.

responses.point: Johansson ranked B026 (circuit QED) first and B038 only sixth, regarding the moire physics as still maturing, and notes the 2025 prize on circuit quantum effects already honoured the superconducting-circuit area.
responses.response: I agree that B026 is a mature, important architecture and that the 2025 prize makes its relationship to a new award a real issue; in my own ranking it is fifth for that reason. I disagree that B038 is premature: independent confirmation within a few years, extension to multiple moire platforms, and the opening of fractional Chern and other topological states point to a field already established. Where I qualify my own position is that B026 is the strongest fallback among the non-condensed-matter candidates if the committee wants distance from graphene.

responses.point: Pearce ranked B016 (IceCube neutrinos) first and accepts a two-name credit, while noting that collaboration size means the decisive individual roles are partly collective.
responses.response: I appreciate that Pearce names the individual-attribution problem for IceCube himself, and it is precisely why I ranked B016 only sixth despite considering the discovery real and large. A two-name prize for a collaboration of hundreds, with source identification of the bulk flux still open, is a weaker case than a prize built on a small number of identifiable authors of the prediction and the experiment. I would not oppose B016 on science, but I would want the committee to be clear about what rests on the diffuse-flux detection versus the source associations.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the pairing mechanism open enough to defer B038, or accepts the platform and correlated-state discovery as sufficient.
Whether Yuan Cao and early twisted-bilayer theorists can be adequately handled within a three-name limit and a carefully worded citation.

How the overlapping topological-insulator entries (B023 and B040) should be packaged or split if the committee prefers condensed matter beyond B038, including the role of Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile; none of the shortlisted credited individuals is among my documented co-authors, supervisors or institutional colleagues, and my neural-network teaching and turbulence work are unrelated to these candidates.
